# Security controls, mapped to MITRE ATT&CK

Every two weeks (and on every change) this project scans itself for
malware, vulnerable dependencies, leaked secrets and insecure code, and
updates what it depends on. This page says *why* each check exists, by
naming the [MITRE ATT&CK](https://attack.mitre.org/) technique it
defends against.

Results appear under the repository's **Security** tab; a failed audit
opens an issue automatically. How to report a problem you find:
[SECURITY.md](../../SECURITY.md).

| Technique | What could go wrong here | How it is stopped |
|---|---|---|
| [T1190](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/) Exploit Public-Facing Application | mn-gui serves HTTP; a flaw in it would be reachable from the browser, or from the network if it were exposed. | Binds to 127.0.0.1 by default and Docker publishes to 127.0.0.1 only; Host header allow-list stops DNS rebinding; JSON-only API with no CORS; strict Content-Security-Policy; 1 MB body, 30 s command and 64 KB output limits; standard library only. |
| [T1195.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/001/) Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools | A vulnerable or malicious dependency (PyPI, apt, a GitHub Action) reaches everyone who installs the project. | Dependabot opens updates weekly; pip-audit and OSV-Scanner check every dependency; dependency review blocks vulnerable additions in pull requests; Actions are pinned to commit SHAs and the base image to a digest. |
| [T1195.002](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/) Compromise Software Supply Chain | Someone publishes an image or a release that looks like ours. | Images are built in CI from a digest-pinned base, signed with cosign (keyless, GitHub OIDC) and published with an SBOM and build provenance; releases come from tags on master. |
| [T1059](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/) Command and Scripting Interpreter | The GUI and the CLI run commands inside emulated hosts as root - that is the product, so it has to be gated. | Every API call needs the 192-bit access token, compared in constant time; commands run without a shell where possible, with a timeout and an output cap; configuration programs run as the user who ran sudo, never as root. |
| [T1068](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/) Exploitation for Privilege Escalation | mnexec is setuid root, and Mininet itself runs as root. | mnexec is built hardened (FORTIFY_SOURCE, stack protector, PIE, RELRO/BIND_NOW), opens files with O_CLOEXEC and parses its arguments strictly; CodeQL scans the C code on every change. |
| [T1105](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/) Ingress Tool Transfer | A file in the repository, or in a published image, carries malware to the people who install it. | ClamAV scans the working tree and the image filesystem every two weeks with fresh signatures. |
| [T1525](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1525/) Implant Internal Image | A backdoor is added to the container image. | Images are rebuilt weekly from scratch with no cache, scanned with Trivy (the build fails on fixable HIGH/CRITICAL), signed, and ship an SBOM anyone can diff. |
| [T1552.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/) Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files | A token or key is committed by accident. | gitleaks scans the full history and Trivy scans the tree for secrets; the GUI token is generated per run and never written to a file. |
| [T1078](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/) Valid Accounts | A workflow token or the GUI token is stolen and reused. | Workflows declare the least privilege they need and check out without persisted credentials; the GUI token travels in the URL fragment, is kept in session storage and never reaches a log, proxy or Referer header. |
| [T1562.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/001/) Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools | A change lands on master without the checks running. | master takes pull requests only, with the test, build and scan checks required and force-pushes blocked; the workflows themselves are scanned by CodeQL (actions) and reviewed by Dependabot. |
| [T1611](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/) Escape to Host | The container runs --privileged, because the emulator needs network namespaces and Open vSwitch. | Documented plainly; the image carries no extra setuid binaries, drops the Open vSwitch PKI from the image, and is meant for a developer machine or a lab VM, not a shared host. |
| [T1565](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1565/) Data Manipulation | The GUI rewrites the lab file; a crash mid-write could destroy a student's work. | Saves are atomic (write to a temporary file in the same directory, then rename) and keep the original owner and mode. |

## The schedule

| When | What runs |
|------|-----------|
| Every change (push, pull request) | Unit, install, Docker, GUI browser and packaging tests; CodeQL (Python, JavaScript, C, Actions); Trivy; pip-audit; dependency review; ShellCheck |
| Every week | Dependabot updates (Actions, pip, base image), a no-cache image rebuild with every pending security patch, and the full test matrix |
| Every two weeks | This audit: ClamAV malware scan, OSV-Scanner, gitleaks over the whole history, a Trivy scan of the published image, and this report |
| Immediately | Dependabot security updates, and GitHub security advisories for anything this project depends on |

Updates that pass every check merge themselves; anything that fails
stops and opens an issue instead.
